subject: HelionWorks SLO & topology — post-call debrief and next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Anya Patel <anya@helionworks.com>, Markus Feld <markus.feld@helionworks.com>
Cc: procurement@helionworks.com
Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: HelionWorks SLO & topology — post-call notes
Attachments: HLW-SLO-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

Thanks again for the productive call today — appreciate the clear context on workloads. Quick recap and agreed next steps so we have the same page:

Summary of pain/goals (as we heard them)
- Primary goal: move latency-sensitive classification + summarization features to a managed inference stack with predictable 95th/99th latency and predictable unit cost.
- Current pain: inconsistent tail latency on current self-hosted setup, spikes during end-of-day batch processes, and limited horizontal scaling.
- Compliance: must run inside a VPC with SOC2 evidence and SSO integration for reviewers.

SLO targets you mentioned
- P95 generation latency: <= 150ms for short prompts (~128 tokens)
- P99 generation latency: <= 450ms for typical user flows
- Target sustained QPS: 40 sustained infer/sec with bursts to 120 for peak windows (estimate ~100 tokens per inference average)
- Throughput footprint: ~3–5M tokens/day expected in steady state; peak/day nearer 6–8M when batch processing runs.

Model & quality notes
- You indicated preference for an instruction-tuned open model and willingness to test a 70B-class quantized variant. We suggested baseline options: rw-instruct-70B (quantized int8), and a 30B low-latency variant for routing fallbacks.
- Important: we should run eval prompts you shared to confirm quality/cost tradeoffs before committing to a rollout.

Topology options discussed
- Private deployment (VPC): recommended for compliance; control plane still hosted, inference nodes in your VPC.
- Dedicated (reserved) capacity: good balance if you want Redwood-managed GPUs but isolated pools.
- Mixed routing: low-latency traffic -> 30B variant on dedicated low-latency nodes; high-throughput/background -> 70B quantized on dedicated/hosted pool.

Immediate next steps (action items)
1) HelionWorks: share 250 sample anonymized requests + one representative batch job (S3 link or staged Drive) — ACTION: Anya
2) HelionWorks: confirm SSO provider and point of contact for procurement (DocuSign timeline) — ACTION: Markus / procurement@helionworks.com
3) Redwood: produce SLO/ops matrix and initial topology diagram + cost ballpark — ACTION: Sean (attached matrix)
4) Redwood Eng request: run a targeted benchmark with the sample payload and quantized models — ACTION: Redwood Eng (Irene)

Proposed timeline
- Share samples by EOD Wed (14 May)
- Benchmarks and initial cost estimate by Wed next week (21 May)
- Technical deep-dive (engineering call) — propose Tue 20 May 10:00 PT

If that aligns, I’ll schedule the technical deep-dive and loop in Marissa from Solutions to cover rollout/CS and procurement coordination.

Thanks — Sean
--
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198
From: Markus Feld <markus.feld@helionworks.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Anya Patel <anya@helionworks.com>
Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 17:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: HelionWorks SLO & topology — post-call notes
Attachments: HelionWorks-internal-topology.pdf (attachment stub)

Thanks Sean — that summary is helpful and accurate. A few clarifications from our side:
- The 40 sustained QPS was per-service endpoint; we actually have 3 endpoints that will be routed through the same cluster (so ~120 sustained QPS aggregate, bursts to 350). I know that changes capacity planning.
- Our batch job runs nightly at 02:00 UTC and generates a large KV-cache warmup pattern; we'd like to avoid impacting latency for live traffic during that window.
- Procurement: procurement@helionworks.com will lead contracting. We need SOC2 evidence and a brief data flow diagram for legal review.

We’ll upload the sample payload (anonymized) to the S3 bucket you provided and share a link by EOD Wed. Also, Anya will confirm specific SSO vendor.

Markus
CTO, HelionWorks
markus.feld@helionworks.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Anya Patel <anya@helionworks.com>, Markus Feld <markus.feld@helionworks.com>
Date: Tue, 13 May 2025 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: HelionWorks SLO & topology — post-call notes (internal asks)

Looping you all in for engineering + CS coordination. Key asks for eng:
- Run a benchmark with the attached HLW-SLO-matrix.xlsx (column with sample sizes) against: rw-instruct-70B (quantized int8) and rw-instruct-30B (low-latency) using HelionWorks sample payload once they upload it. Capture P50/P95/P99 and tokens/sec, and include KV-cache hit/miss profile.
- Simulate 3 endpoints (combined sustained ~120 QPS, bursts to 350) and a concurrent nightly batch job pattern that warms KV caches. Show latency impact and potential mitigation (separate pools, autoscale buffers).
- Provide a draft cost model for: private VPC nodes (customer-managed infra), Redwood Dedicated reserved pool, and a hybrid routing config. Include rough GPU-hour estimates and expected cost per 1000 tokens.

Marissa — please prepare a short procurement checklist (SOC2 artifacts, SSO docs, DocuSign timeline) so we can share with Markus/procurement. Rishi — heads up in case we want to propose an early commitment discount if they push for reserved capacity after benchmarking.

I’ll schedule the 20 May engineering deep-dive unless you object.

Thanks,
Sean
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 May 2025 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: HelionWorks SLO & topology — post-call notes (internal asks)

Received — planning to spin up a small benchmark cluster today. Notes / prelim actions:
- Will run two model variants (70B quantized int8, 30B fp16) against a 1k-sample smoke set immediately and share results by EOD Wed (14 May).
- For capacity sims: will use k8s-based autoscale profile with separate node pools to emulatemixed routing. I’ll include KV-cache hit-rate toggles to observe tail-latency effects.
- Need: HelionWorks S3 link + anonymized schema doc. Also confirm target p99 latency budget (you wrote 450ms, Markus mentioned tight peaks — please confirm if p99 can stretch to 600ms during sustained nightly warmups or if that is a hard limit).

I’ll attach preliminary numbers and a one-page runbook for the 20 May call.

Irene
Senior Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference
